title: Bug: [orchagent] SIGSEGV in AclRange::remove due to infinite loop in error-handling path
author: ashishalok-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific
yes

### Importance or Severity
Critical

### Description of the bug

A SIGSEGV occurs in orchagent within the AclRange::remove function. The crash is caused by a logic error in a for loop where the loop boundary variable is incremented instead of the iterator, leading to an infinite loop and eventual out-of-bounds memory access.

**To Reproduce**

1. Attempt to create an ACL rule (e.g., EVERFLOW) on a platform where the specific attribute combination is not supported by the SAI (returning SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED).

2. The AclRule::createRule fails and enters the cleanup path.

3. AclRange::remove is called to clean up range objects.

4. The process crashes immediately.

**Expected behavior**: The AclRange::remove function should iterate through the range OIDs exactly once, perform the cleanup, and allow orchagent to log the SAI error and continue running.

**Actual behavior**: The process terminates with signal SIGSEGV.

**Log portions**:
`ERR swss#orchagent: :- createRule: Failed to create ACL rule RULE_1, rv:-2`
`ERR swss#orchagent: :- create: create status: SAI_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`
`INFO swss#supervisord 2026-01-21 16:21:35,462 WARN exited: orchagent (terminated by SIGSEGV (core dumped); not expected) `

linkedPullRequests.author: ashishalok-arista
linkedPullRequests.body:
This patch is to fix a major bug in the for loop of the function AclRange::remove.

<!--

3. Make sure your commit message contains enough details about the change and related tests
4. Make sure your pull request adds related reviewers, asignees, labels

Please also provide the following information in this pull request:
-->

**What I did**
Fixed a critical logic error in AclRange::remove where the loop limit (oidsCnt) was being incremented instead of the loop index (oidIdx).

**Why I did it**
The original code contained an infinite loop: for (int oidIdx = 0; oidIdx < oidsCnt; oidsCnt++). This caused Memory Corruption/Crash: The loop would continue until oidsCnt accessed memory outside the bounds of the oids pointer, resulting in a SIGSEGV (Segmentation Fault).

**How I verified it**
After the fix, orchagent remains stable and correctly logs the SAI error (rv:-2) instead of terminating.

**Details if related**
The crash was specifically observed in Arista Gardena switches.

### Issues
Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/issues/4174
Fixes: [sonic-qual.msft](https://github.com/aristanetworks/sonic-qual.msft/issues/1067)

Already fixed in 202511: #4173
